# trafficserver / fuzz_yamlcpp

trafficserver's own fuzz target `fuzz_yamlcpp` ([source](source/fuzz_yamlcpp.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over trafficserver (apache/trafficserver at 97d2831f).

Copies the input (size_data from 8 to 1024 bytes) into a string and parses it with yaml-cpp's YAML::Load, catching and dropping every exception (catch (...)), and drops the parsed node. It returns -1 for an input with size_data below 8 or above 1024.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against trafficserver at commit 97d2831f with 3 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/fuzz_yamlcpp.cc is trafficserver 97d2831f's tests/fuzzing/fuzz_yamlcpp.cc with one Theorem Labs change: its length check returns -1, not 1, for an input outside its limits (libFuzzer rejects the input; the driver exits 0, not 78).

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch trafficserver` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.
